prompt: An editor replaces plain list assignment with a full list slice. Each complete program starts fresh and performs only the shown inner-list append. Do the two programs print the same line, and which explanation of the outer and inner lists is correct? Compare these exact programs, not every possible later operation.

options.text: Yes. Both print [[1], [2]], because append returns a new inner list and does not change its receiver.
options.feedback: append changes its receiver. In both programs copied[0] refers to the original first inner list, so appending 9 changes rows[0]. Both actually print [[1, 9], [2]].

options.text: No. Plain assignment prints [[1, 9], [2]], but the slice prints [[1], [2]] because slicing also copies the inner lists.
options.feedback: A full list slice copies the outer container, not the nested lists. Its first element still refers to the original first inner list, so the slice program also prints [[1, 9], [2]].

options.text: Yes. Both print [[1, 9], [2]], because a full slice returns the same outer list, exactly like plain assignment.
options.feedback: Both complete outputs are right, but the outer-list claim is wrong. A full slice makes a new outer list whose elements refer to the existing inner lists. Sharing the first inner list is enough for this append to affect rows.
options.partial_reason: Both programs print exactly [[1, 9], [2]], so their shown outputs match. The claim that slicing returns the same outer list is wrong: it creates a new outer list with references to the existing inner lists.

options.text: Yes. Both print [[1, 9], [2]]. The slice creates a new outer list, but both programs still reach the same original inner list at index 0.
options.feedback: Correct. Plain assignment shares the outer list too; slicing does not. Nevertheless both share the first inner list with rows, and that is the object append changes here.

options.text: Neither prints a line: both raise TypeError while creating rows, because a list cannot contain mutable lists as elements.
options.feedback: Lists may contain other lists. Mutable elements are allowed; dictionary-key hashability restrictions do not apply to list elements. Both programs run and print [[1, 9], [2]].

explanation: Plain assignment gives rows and copied the same outer list. A full slice creates a different outer list but copies references to its elements, not the inner lists themselves. Therefore copied[0] in either program is the original first inner list. append mutates that list, so both programs print [[1, 9], [2]]. Matching this inner-mutation output does not mean the outer containers are identical or that all later operations would be equivalent.

verification.rationale: Execute both exact displayed programs independently. Their complete outputs match for this shown operation. Human object-reference reasoning distinguishes new-outer/shared-inner semantics from the incorrect same-outer explanation, which happens to predict the same outputs.
verification.limitations: Equal traces here are not a general proof of equivalence or an identity test for the outer lists. No hidden identity-check program is executed. Half credit, distractor appeal and difficulty remain editorial and uncalibrated.
